_fixture: what scan-page.js produces for tests/fixtures/hostile/forms/consent-decoupled.html — REGENERATED by running the real scanner over the served page (tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs holds it to that).
_labelExact: g1 has NO labelExact: its label comes from an aria-label, and an attribute is not text the user can read, so an attribute can never establish exactness. g2/g3/g4 have labelExact:true and their `l` is UNTRUNCATED — which is what makes g2 and g3 distinguishable again. Before the vouch they both sliced to the same 120 characters and the allowlist could not tell a certification from a jury-trial waiver. The OPTION under a vouched group carries that same untruncated string (scan-page.js: `l: g.labelExact ? own : txt(own, 80)`); the hand-written version of this file cut the two long options at 120, which is a shape the scanner cannot produce.
_g5: g5 (#consent-transparent) was MISSING from the hand-written version of this file for the whole life of the fixture. The served page has always carried it and board-fidelity.test.mjs has always asserted the trait is on the page — but no consumer test ever saw the field, because it was not in the scan. On a machine with no browser, tests/security/browser-vouch.test.mjs skips, so the color:transparent carrier reached NO consumer at all. Its label is visually identical text hidden from the eye; scan-page.js refuses the vouch with labelWhy 'label text is not visibly rendered'.
_forged: A page-supplied scanner can put labelExact:true on anything (see tests/security/rce-round-trip.test.mjs). This fixture is what the REAL scanner produces; the forged variant is constructed inside the test that needs it.
